extraction.name: LUMA
extraction.description: LUMA is a multimodal dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data. It enables the controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, Sébastien Foumier
extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Foumier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Leaming from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th Intemational ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR ’25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were compiled from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset. Audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels were extracted and validated from three diverse audio corpora, plus 73 voluntary contributions. Text data was generated based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model (LLM).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10 datasets (images); The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice corpora, along with voluntary contributions (audio); Google's Gemma-7B Instruct model (text).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A Python toolkit allows the injection of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties by controlling data diversity (sampling based on inverse distance to class center), adding sample noise (background noise for audio, text perturbations via nlpaug, image perturbations), injecting label noise (randomly altering labels to semantically close classes), and injecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio samples were automatically validated using Whisper Large V3, and false negatives were manually validated. Text samples were validated by masking label occurrences and feeding the text back into Gemma-7B Instruct to check if the prediction matched the ground truth label.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For audio classes with fewer than 800 samples, manual validation was performed. Annotators were presented with an audio sample and the prompt 'Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra s or es in the pronunciation is okay.)' and asked to answer 'Yes' or 'No'.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The manual validation process achieved a 71.61% annotation agreement. Samples were accepted only if both annotators confirmed their validity; samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model (audio transcription/validation), Google's Gemma-7B Instruct model (text generation, validation, and bias detection).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender (identified during bias analysis of generated text for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl').
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote and support the development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches, helping the research community design safer machine learning approaches for safety-critical applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The generated text modality contains offensive biases and stereotypes, particularly a large amount of gender bias for the classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl'.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Because the textual data was generated using an LLM, the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data, Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, and studying uncertainty quantification in multimodal classification settings.
